ops.description:
Adversarial review of the bindings (2026-07-18, refuter-confirmed parity-5/6) found the gemini-family argv shape treats a leading-dash prompt as a flag: plans emit `-p <prompt>`, and empirically `gemini -p --help` shows help instead of treating `--help` as the prompt; `agy` parses `-p` as a boolean alias for `--print`, so the prompt rides as a positional and a leading-dash prompt is eaten.

Fix discipline (CORE-FIRST — updated for the 0.9.0 oracle inversion, note 54e3156b): change `rust/spawnllm-core/src/plan/{gemini,antigravity}.rs` to a dash-safe delivery (e.g. `--` terminator if the CLIs support it, verified against both installed CLIs), regenerate the vectors (`cargo run -p conformance-gen -- --write`), commit core + vectors together, and confirm strict conformance plus all three host replays stay green (`cargo test --workspace`, `go test ./...`, `uv run pytest tests/test_conformance_replay.py`). Python needs NO separate port — it inherits through the wasm blob; rebuild it (`task blob`). Low urgency: gemini is never auto-selected and claude/codex deliver prompts via stdin, so only explicit gemini/agy runs with dash-leading prompts misbehave.
